# nirvana_networking_firewall_rule (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nirvana_networking_firewall_rule" "example_networking_firewall_rule" {
  vpc_id = "vpc_id"
  destination_address = "10.0.0.0/25"
  destination_ports = ["22", "80", "443"]
  name = "my-firewall-rule"
  protocol = "tcp"
  source_address = "0.0.0.0/0"
  tags = ["production", "ethereum"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination_address` (String) Destination address of the Firewall Rule. Either VPC CIDR or VM in VPC. Must be in network-aligned/canonical form.
- `destination_ports` (List of String) Destination ports of the Firewall Rule.
- `name` (String) Name of the Firewall Rule.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol of the Firewall Rule.
Available values: "tcp", "udp".
- `source_address` (String) Source address of the Firewall Rule. Address of 0.0.0.0 requires a CIDR mask of 0. Must be in network-aligned/canonical form.
- `vpc_id` (String)

### Optional

- `tags` (List of String) Tags to attach to the Firewall Rule.

### Read-Only

- `action` (String) What the Firewall Rule does with the traffic it matches. Rules you create allow traffic.
Available values: "allow", "deny".
- `created_at` (String) When the Firewall Rule was created.
- `direction` (String) Direction of the traffic the Firewall Rule matches. Rules you create are ingress rules.
Available values: "ingress", "egress".
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the Operation.
- `managed_by` (Attributes) What manages the resource, or null when nothing does. A managed resource can be read but not changed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--managed_by))
- `project_id` (String) Project ID the Operation belongs to.
- `status` (String) Status of the resource.
Available values: "pending", "creating", "updating", "ready", "deleting", "deleted", "error", "suspended".
- `updated_at` (String) When the Firewall Rule was updated.

<a id="nestedatt--managed_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `managed_by`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) ID of the thing managing the resource. For a vpc_egress_policy, the ID of the VPC.
- `type` (String) Kind of thing managing the resource. A vpc_egress_policy manages the Firewall Rules that block outbound traffic to ports commonly used for abuse.
Available values: "sandbox_cluster", "vpc_egress_policy".

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import nirvana_networking_firewall_rule.example '<vpc_id>/<firewall_rule_id>'
```
